title: Plugins, Apps & Hooks
description: codex plugin installs bundled skills/MCP/prompts from marketplace snapshots, hooks fire on lifecycle events, and codex mcp-server turns Codex itself into a callable tool.

steps.annotation: A marketplace is a source (local path or Git repo) of plugin snapshots; `marketplace add` registers it in config before anything is installed.
codex plugin add installs a plugin from a configured marketplace snapshot into local config and cache. The `plugins` feature flag is stable and on by default.

steps.content: install: unpack skills/ + mcp_servers + prompts from the snapshot -> merge into the resolved Config
steps.annotation: A plugin is a bundle: it contributes skills, MCP servers, and prompt presets that resolve through the same config chain as hand-written config.
Back in the loop, the installed plugin's skill is now eligible to load, exactly as if it had been added by hand.
Hooks are user commands bound to lifecycle events; the harness runs them at the event, not the model. --dangerously-bypass-hook-trust skips the persisted trust check for automation.

steps.content: I'll load the reviewer skill, then walk the diff.
steps.annotation: The skill the plugin shipped is injected on demand; the loop itself is unchanged.
Plugin-contributed tools and MCP servers are dispatched by the same tool layer as built-ins.

steps.content: elsewhere: argv = [codex, mcp-server]  ->  Codex starts AS an MCP server over stdio
steps.annotation: codex mcp-server exposes the harness itself as a tool, so another agent or IDE can call Codex through the standard MCP protocol.

steps.content: Review done via the plugin's skill; Codex can also serve other tools as an MCP server.
steps.annotation: Plugins and hooks extend Codex from the inside; mcp-server exposes it to the outside. The agent loop stays the single constant.
